page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Racemose
lines: indefinitely; it never ends in a flower.
The flowers are arranged in acropetal order -
oldest at the base, youngest at the tip.
steps.why: One fact decides everything: the axis keeps growing. Because the tip stays a growing point, new (young) flowers keep appearing at the top - acropetal order.
common_mistakes: Writing basipetal for racemose. Acropetal order follows from the growing tip.
steps.memory_tip: Racemose keeps rising; acropetal - apex youngest.
steps.margin_note: Growth of the axis + flower order + one example.

steps.label: Cymose

lines.text: Cymose: the peduncle ends in a flower, so

lines: The flowers are arranged in basipetal order -
youngest at the base side, oldest at the top.
steps.why: The cymose axis is used up by its terminal flower, so growth stops and later flowers appear below it - basipetal order. Each column of the table mirrors the other.
common_mistakes: Writing that the cymose axis grows indefinitely - that is the racemose character.
steps.memory_tip: Cymose closes with a flower; basipetal - the base gets the young ones.
steps.margin_note: Mirror the racemose column point for point; the book's example spelling is 'Jasminun' - write Jasminum.
